conditions: Maximum 30 days, non-extendable, non-convertible
Singapore permanent residents (any nationality) qualify only through designated immigration checkpoints
description: Visa-free short visit for citizens of 19 countries/special-administrative-region governments plus foreign holders of Singapore permanent residence entering via designated checkpoints. Stay is a maximum of 30 days and cannot be extended or converted to another stay permit. Base regulation Perpres 95/2024; Brazil and Turkey added by Permenimipas 9/2025 effective 2025-07-03; Peru, Kazakhstan, Macau SAR and Belarus added by Permenimipas 10/2026 (Berita Negara 2026 No. 463, promulgated 2026-07-09). Permitted purposes include tourism, business meetings, and medical treatment.
policy_name: Bebas Visa Kunjungan (BVK) — Visit Visa Exemption

conditions: Fee IDR 500,000; extendable once (30+30 days)
e-VOA applications online at evisa.imigrasi.go.id (87 passports listed there, additionally including San Marino; a few countries on the 97-country border-VOA list are absent from the e-VOA list)
Passport valid at least 6 months from arrival
description: Citizens of 97 listed countries/entities may obtain a Visitor Visa on arrival (or online in advance as e-VOA via evisa.imigrasi.go.id, which lists 87 eligible passports) for tourism, government visits, business meetings, goods purchasing, or transit. 30-day stay, extendable once for another 30 days. Fee IDR 500,000. Single entry; visa validity 90 days from issuance; designated entry points published by the Directorate General of Immigration.
maximum_stay: 30 days, extendable once for a further 30 days
policy_name: Visa on Arrival (VoA) / electronic Visa on Arrival (e-VOA)

conditions: Apply online at evisa.imigrasi.go.id
Profit-making activities prohibited; visit purposes only
Nationals of Calling Visa countries are subject to a special approval procedure (see special_regime policy)
description: Official online visa system of the Directorate General of Immigration. Tourist visit eVisa allows a stay of up to 60 days, extendable, fee IDR 1,500,000, processed in about 5 working days, must be used within 90 days of issuance; proof of living cost of at least USD 2,000 required. This is the default pre-travel channel for nationalities not eligible for visa exemption or Visa on Arrival (embassy guidance indicates a sponsor in Indonesia is required for such applicants).
policy_name: Indonesia eVisa (tourist visit visa) via evisa.imigrasi.go.id

conditions: Special approval procedure; details not published on the fetched official pages
description: Citizens of certain countries deemed to require special scrutiny ('Calling Visa' subjects) cannot use standard visa channels; per the Directorate General of Immigration office pages the current list is Afghanistan, Israel, North Korea, Liberia, Nigeria, Somalia. The specific application procedure is not described on the official pages fetched.
policy_name: Calling Visa

conditions: Tourism and other Temporary Visitor activities only; no paid work, long-term study or residency.
GBR entry limited to British citizens.
IDN and ARE subject to registration/travel-authorization conditions per the ISA list; details unverified.
Canonical per-country stay periods are published by MOFA (novisa.html), which was unreachable (HTTP 403); list here may be missing entries (e.g. Hungary).
description: Japan maintains visa-exemption measures for nationals of listed countries/regions for short-term stays (Temporary Visitor status: tourism, recreation, visiting relatives, sightseeing, meetings, business liaison and similar activities; no paid work). The ISA 'specified country' list enumerates the countries/regions for which Japan currently maintains visa-exemption measures, excluding countries whose exemption is temporarily suspended or subject to visa-obtainment-recommendation measures. Period of stay is granted in units of up to 90, 30 or 15 days; JNTO states most nationalities receive up to 90 days.
maximum_stay: up to 90 days (units of 90, 30 or 15 days depending on nationality)
policy_name: Japan short-term stay visa exemption arrangements (査証免除措置)

conditions: Details of consular procedures, fees, accredited travel-agency requirements (e.g. for Chinese nationals) and any mandated visa application centers could not be verified: MOFA and emb-japan.go.jp sites returned HTTP 403.
description: Foreign nationals not covered by a visa-exemption arrangement must hold a valid passport and obtain a visa before travel. Per ISA: nationals of visa-exempt countries/regions need no visa; all others require one. JNTO describes the application (form, valid passport, photo, accommodation/itinerary, proof of funds) with processing typically around five business days, and refers applicants to Japanese embassies/consulates via the MOFA directory.
maximum_stay: granted in units of up to 90, 30 or 15 days (Temporary Visitor status)
policy_name: Short-term stay (Temporary Visitor) visa via Japanese overseas missions

conditions: Not yet in force; scope of covered nationalities (expected to target visa-exempt travelers) not specified on the fetched page.
description: The Reiwa-8 (2026) amendment to the Immigration Control Act creates JESTA, an electronic travel authorization system. The creating provisions take effect on a date to be fixed by cabinet order no later than 31 March 2029 (令和11年3月31日). JESTA is NOT operational as of 2026-07-23; no traveler currently needs or can obtain a Japanese ETA.
policy_name: JESTA (Japan Electronic System for Travel Authorization) — enacted, not yet in force

conditions: Business and tourism purposes only
Valid ticket for return journey to port of origin or next port of destination
Passport valid for at least six (6) months beyond the contemplated period of stay
Brazil and Israel: 59 days pursuant to bilateral agreements
description: Nationals of 157 countries (155 at 30 days plus Brazil and Israel at 59 days) may enter the Philippines without a visa for business and tourism, provided they hold valid return/onward tickets and passports valid at least six months beyond the contemplated stay. Initial 30-day admission is extendable through Bureau of Immigration visa waiver (first extension 29 days) and further extensions up to 36 months total for non-visa-required nationals.
policy_name: Executive Order No. 408 (as amended) visa-free entry for temporary visitors

conditions: Non-extendible and non-convertible
Tourism and business purposes
Designated ports of entry only: NAIA (Metro Manila) and Mactan-Cebu International Airport (Cebu)
description: Chinese nationals may enter the Philippines without a visa for a non-extendible and non-convertible period of 14 days for tourism and business purposes, effective 16 January 2026, only through Ninoy Aquino International Airport and Mactan-Cebu International Airport. Separately, mainland Chinese tourists holding a valid Australian, Japanese, Canadian, Schengen or US visa may enter for 7 days, extendable to 21 days total.
policy_name: Visa-free entry for Chinese nationals (14 days)

conditions: 14 days: passport valid 6+ months beyond stay, confirmed hotel booking, proof of financial capacity, return/onward ticket
30 days: valid AJACSSUK visa or residence permit, passport valid 6+ months, return/onward ticket
Non-extendible, non-convertible; no derogatory record with the Bureau of Immigration
description: Effective 8 June 2025, Indian nationals may enter visa-free for a non-extendible, non-convertible 14-day period for tourism (passport 6+ months validity, confirmed hotel booking, proof of financial capacity, return/onward ticket). Indian nationals holding valid AJACSSUK (American, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, Schengen, Singapore, UK) visas or residence permits may enter visa-free for a non-extendible 30-day period. Available at any Philippine port of entry; no derogatory BI record.
policy_name: Visa-free privileges for Indian nationals

conditions: Initial admission 14 days for HK SAR and Macau SAR passports
Hong Kong British passports: 7 days, extendable to 21 days; Macau-Portuguese passports: 7 days initial admission per BI
description: Hong Kong SAR passport holders and Macau SAR passport holders may enter the Philippines visa-free for an initial stay of fourteen (14) days. Holders of Hong Kong British (BNO) and Macau-Portuguese passports receive 7 days initial admission (Hong Kong British extendable to 21 days).
policy_name: Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR passport holders

conditions: Tourism applicants (9(a-2)) need flight reservations for entry and exit, proof of financial capacity, proof of ties to home country, hotel/lodging proof; parental permission for minors traveling alone
The e-Visa is not a guarantee of admission
description: Online application platform for the 9(a) Temporary Visitor Visa (subtypes 9(a-1) business through 9(a-8) other purposes, including 9(a-2) Tourism/Leisure), developed by DFA with DICT, DOT, NICA, BI and DOJ. Processing 7-12 working days (single entry) and 15-21 working days (multiple entry). e-Visas are not convertible to other visa types and not valid for extension of the authorized stay. The list of eligible citizenships/countries of residence is rendered dynamically on the portal and could not be verified from static pages.
policy_name: Philippine e-Visa (eVisaPH)

conditions: More stringent documentary requirements per Philippine Codified Visa Rules and Regulations
Onward ticket departing within 59 days of arrival (visa-free nationals) or 30 days (non-visa-free nationals)
Fees are non-refundable
description: Nationals of countries not included in EO 408 (as amended) are visa-required and apply for the 9(a) Temporary Visitor Visa at Philippine Foreign Service Posts. Fee tiers at the Embassy in Washington DC: visa-free nationals USD 30/60/90, non-visa-free nationals USD 40/80/120, Chinese nationals USD 25/50/100 (single 3-month / multiple 6-month / multiple 1-year validity). Visa-required nationals admitted on 9(a) may extend stay with the BI up to 24 months.
maximum_stay: 59 days per admission; extendable up to 24 months (visa-required) / 36 months (non-visa-required)
policy_name: 9(a) Temporary Visitor Visa via Philippine embassies and consulates

conditions: Initial visa waiver package fee P3,030 (Visa Waiver P500, Application P1,000, Certification P500, Legal Research P30, Express P1,000)
Overstay penalty P500 per month
description: Non-visa-required tourists admitted for 30 days may obtain an initial 29-day visa waiver extension (total 59 days) and further extensions of 1, 2 or 6 months, up to 36 months total stay; visa-required nationals may extend up to 24 months. Apply at least one week before the current stay expires; also available online via BI e-Services.
policy_name: Bureau of Immigration Temporary Visitor (9A) Visa Waiver and Tourist Visa Extension

conditions: Details (eligible nationalities, sponsorship/accreditation requirements, fees) not verified from fetched official pages
description: The BI FAQ lists Visa Upon Arrival options including a 30-day Visa Upon Arrival, group tours under a Memorandum Order, and a Pro-Investment Visa under a Memorandum Circular. Eligibility criteria, covered nationalities and fees are not detailed on the fetched official pages.
policy_name: Visa Upon Arrival (VUA) programs

conditions: Visa-required countries/places: Afghanistan, Algeria, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Belarus, DPR Korea, Egypt, Georgia, India, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kyrgyzstan, Lebanon, Libya, Mali, Moldova, Morocco, Nigeria, Pakistan, Russia, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tunisia, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Yemen

Visa-required document types regardless of nationality: refugee travel documents, alien's passports, Palestinian Authority passports, temporary UAE passports, Hong Kong SAR Documents of Identity, Macao SAR Travel Permits, PRC Travel Documents
description: ICA publishes the exhaustive list of countries/places whose travel-document holders require a Singapore entry visa (34 countries plus specified special travel documents). Nationals of all other countries do not require a visa for social/tourist visits. The period of stay is determined by the Visit Pass (e-Pass) issued at the checkpoint upon entry, not by any visa.
policy_name: Singapore entry visa requirement list (negative list; all others visa-exempt)

conditions: Ordinary PRC passports only
PRC diplomatic, public affairs and service passport holders were already exempt under long-standing agreements
description: With effect from 9 February 2024, holders of ordinary passports issued by the PRC are exempted from visa requirements for a stay of up to 30 days in Singapore. Holders of all other PRC-issued travel documents must continue to apply for an entry visa before travel.
policy_name: Mutual 30-Day Visa-Exemption Arrangement between Singapore and the People's Republic of China

conditions: S$30 non-refundable processing fee (online, Visa or MasterCard credit/debit card)
Processing within three working days excluding day of submission; some applications may take longer
The visa is pre-entry permission; period of stay is set by the Visit Pass (e-Pass) issued on entry
description: Visa-required nationals must obtain a Singapore entry visa before travel. Applications are submitted online via ICA's SAVE e-Service through a local contact in Singapore or an authorised strategic partner/visa agent, or at a Singapore Overseas Mission or through its authorised visa agent. ICA does not accept visa applications at the immigration counters. In China, missions have ceased walk-in applications since 8 December 2014 and applications go through Authorised Visa Agents.
policy_name: Singapore entry visa (pre-travel application; issued electronically)

conditions: Transit to/from a third country; eligibility subject to specific conditions assessed by ICA
Stays under 96 hours
description: Nationals of the Commonwealth of Independent States, Georgia, India, Turkmenistan and Ukraine, as well as selected nationals of the People's Republic of China, may be eligible for visa-free transit through Singapore for up to 96 hours under specific conditions (transit only; not a tourist-entry channel).
policy_name: Visa-Free Transit Facility (VFTF)

conditions: Submit within 3 days (including day of arrival) before arriving
Not a visa; does not replace visa requirements
description: All travellers are required to submit the SG Arrival Card within three days (including the day of arrival) before arriving in Singapore. The SG Arrival Card is not a visa. Exceptions apply to those transiting without immigration clearance and to citizens/residents entering via land checkpoints.
policy_name: SG Arrival Card (SGAC)

conditions: Passport valid at least 6 months
Proof of onward travel to leave Thailand within 60 days of arrival
Funds of 20,000 THB per person / 40,000 THB per family
TDAC submission within 3 days before arrival
description: Nationals of 93 countries and territories are entitled to visa exemption for tourism and short-term business engagements for up to 60 days per entry, extendable once by up to 30 days at the discretion of the Immigration Bureau. Re-entrants may stay a cumulative maximum of 90 days within 6 months of first entry. Effective 15 July 2024. A Cabinet decision of 19 May 2026 (revised 14 July 2026) approved replacing this scheme with 30-day and 15-day exemption lists, pending Royal Gazette publication; not yet in effect as of 2026-07-23.
maximum_stay: 60 days, extendable by up to 30 days; cumulative 90 days within 6 months on re-entry
policy_name: Tourist Visa Exemption Scheme (60 days)

conditions: Tourism purpose only
Fee 2,000 THB
Single entry
TDAC submission within 3 days before arrival
description: Nationals of 31 countries and territories may apply for a single-entry Visa on Arrival at immigration checkpoints for tourism, for a stay not exceeding 15 days, fee 2,000 THB. Revised list effective 15 July 2024. A Cabinet decision of 19 May 2026 (revised 14 July 2026) approved cutting the list to a handful of countries, pending Royal Gazette publication; not yet in effect as of 2026-07-23.
policy_name: Visa on Arrival (VoA) for tourism

conditions: Application submitted online via thaievisa.go.th to the competent Royal Thai Embassy/Consulate-General
Some nationalities must apply only in their home/residence country
description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs operates the official Thai eVisa platform at https://www.thaievisa.go.th/ through which visa applications (including the TR tourist visa and METV) are submitted online to Royal Thai Embassies and Consulates-General. Embassy pages (e.g. Sydney, Helsinki) direct applicants to apply through this e-Visa system; payment online by Visa or Mastercard.
policy_name: Thai eVisa (electronic visa application system)

conditions: Passport minimum 6 months validity (TR); 12 months and 2 blank pages (METV)
Evidence of travel from Thailand (air ticket paid in full)
Financial proof: 20,000 THB per person / 40,000 THB per family (TR); bank statement requirements for METV set by mission
description: TR tourist visa: fee 1,000 THB per entry, visa validity 3 or 6 months, permitted stay up to 60 days per entry, extendable by up to 30 days. METV: visa validity 6 months, stay up to 60 days per entry; fee charged in local currency by the mission (e.g. 170 EUR at the Royal Thai Embassy Helsinki; TR at Helsinki 40 EUR). METV requires passport validity of not less than 12 months on arrival and at least two empty visa pages, plus financial evidence.
policy_name: Tourist Visa TR (single entry) and Multiple Entry Tourist Visa (METV)

conditions: Submit online within 3 days before arrival
Entry will not be processed by the immigration officer without it
description: Since 1 May 2025, all non-Thai nationals must complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card online at https://tdac.immigration.go.th within 3 days before arrival. It replaces the paper TM.6 arrival card and is required for immigration processing regardless of visa category. It is an arrival card, not a visa or travel authorization.
policy_name: Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC)

conditions: Takes effect 15 days after Royal Gazette publication (not yet published)
Transition: those entering before the effective date keep their permitted stay
description: On 19 May 2026 the Thai Cabinet approved revoking the 60-day visa exemption scheme for all 93 countries/territories, moving to a 30-day tourism visa exemption list (initially 54 countries/territories; per the revised 14 July 2026 Cabinet decision reported by the Tourism Authority of Thailand, 59 countries/territories including all 27 EU member states, India, Croatia, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Malta and the Maldives), a new 15-day exemption (Mauritius and Seychelles), and a sharply reduced VoA list (Azerbaijan, Belarus, Serbia). The Ministry of Interior announcements remain pending publication in the Royal Gazette and take effect 15 days after publication. As of 2026-07-23 the changes are NOT in force; current entry conditions remain in place. Travellers entering before the effective date may stay until expiry of their permitted period of stay.
policy_name: Approved 2026 revision of visa exemption and VoA schemes (PENDING, not in force)

conditions: Regardless of passport type and purpose of entry
Must fully meet entry conditions prescribed by Viet Nam's laws
description: 45-day visa-free entry regardless of passport type and purpose of entry for citizens of 12 countries, extended from 15 March 2025 to 14 March 2028.
maximum_stay: 45 days from the date of entry
policy_name: Unilateral visa exemption for 12 countries (Resolution No. 44/NQ-CP)

conditions: Tourism purpose
Regardless of passport type
Must meet Viet Nam's legal entry requirements
description: 45-day visa-free entry for tourism purpose, regardless of passport type, for citizens of 12 European countries; supersedes Resolution No. 11/NQ-CP (15 January 2025) which covered Poland, Czech Republic and Switzerland.
maximum_stay: 45 days from the date of entry
policy_name: Tourism Development Stimulus Program exemption for 12 European countries (Resolution No. 229/NQ-CP)

conditions: Stay per bilateral treaty; 30-day temporary residence period where treaty is silent
description: Visa-free entry under bilateral agreements for ASEAN members and several other states, as listed on the official Vietnam tourism board site. Stay duration follows the applicable treaty; where the treaty does not specify, a 30-day temporary residence period is granted per official government guidance. Per-country durations were not verifiable from fetched official pages.
policy_name: Bilateral/treaty visa exemptions

conditions: Applicant must be outside Vietnam and hold a valid passport
Not in visa-suspension categories under Article 21 of Vietnam's immigration law
Fee paid via electronic payment gateway; not refunded if the application is refused
description: Electronic visa issued by the Vietnamese Immigration Department (Ministry of Public Security) to citizens of all countries and territories since 15 August 2023. Valid for a maximum of 90 days, single or multiple entry. Fee US$25 single entry / US$50 multiple entry, non-refundable. Processed in 3 working days. Usable at 83 designated border gates (expanded December 2025).
policy_name: Viet Nam E-visa (universal)

conditions: Passport with at least 06 months of validity prior to the proposed date of entry
Completed application form, photo(s), and fee payment required
description: Visas may be applied for in person or by mail at Vietnamese diplomatic missions (e.g. the Embassy in Washington DC). Fees vary by visa type, duration and service level; standard processing 6-7 working days without approval letter, faster with one.
policy_name: Consular visa at Vietnamese embassies/consulates

conditions: Eligibility limited to designated priority groups; approval by competent authorities
description: Multiple-entry special visa exemption card for designated groups (official guests, scholars/experts, investors, cultural/arts/sports figures, honorary consuls, other approved special cases). Validity up to five years and at least 30 days shorter than the passport's remaining validity. Not a general tourist channel.
policy_name: Special visa exemption card for priority visitors (Decree No. 221/2025/ND-CP)

conditions: TWN eligible only with a Taiwan passport that includes the personal identification card number
Not needed by holders of British or Irish passports or people with permission to live, work or study in the UK
Does not guarantee entry
description: Digital permission to travel (not a visa) required by non-visa nationals visiting the UK, Jersey, Guernsey or the Isle of Man for up to 6 months, or transiting through UK border control. Costs £20, valid 2 years or until passport expiry, unlimited entries, linked to one passport. Apply via the UK ETA app or online at GOV.UK.
policy_name: UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)

conditions: Exceptions (VN 2.2): Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passport holders, and Taiwan passports containing the national ID card number, are not visa nationals
Exemptions for school groups from France (18 and under) and Germany (19 and under)
Earliest application 3 months before travel; decision usually within 3 weeks
description: Nationals of the 115 countries/territories on the Immigration Rules Appendix Visitor: Visa national list (including China, India, Russia, Turkey) must obtain a Standard Visitor visa (entry clearance) before travelling to the UK for tourism. Application is online via GOV.UK followed by biometric enrolment at an overseas visa application centre (operated by VFS Global). £135 for up to 6 months; long-term options 2/5/10 years.
policy_name: Standard Visitor visa / Appendix Visitor: Visa national list

conditions: Irish citizens travel within the Common Travel Area
description: Holders of British or Irish passports need neither a visa nor an ETA to enter the UK. People who already hold permission to live, work or study in the UK also do not need an ETA.
policy_name: British and Irish passport holder exemption

conditions: Tourism / visit / transit purposes only; no remunerative activity
K-ETA rules apply to visa-free entrants (see eta_program)
The full official list (100+ countries) is maintained on k-eta.go.kr and government portals; the applies_to list here contains only the nationalities verified during this research
description: Nationals of countries with which Korea has concluded visa waiver agreements, and nationals of countries designated for visa-free entry by presidential decree (international friendship / tourism / national interest), may enter without a visa under B-1 (visa exemption) or B-2 (tourism/transit) status, generally for up to 90 days (some countries 30 or 60 days; Canada 6 months). Paid activities are not permitted.
maximum_stay: Typically 90 days; 30/60 days for some countries; 6 months for Canada; Russia 60 days per entry (90/180)
policy_name: Visa waiver agreements and designated visa-free entry (B-1 / B-2)

conditions: Applies only to nationals eligible for visa-free entry; visa holders do not need K-ETA
Exempt regardless of nationality: diplomatic/official passport holders, UN laissez-passer holders, ABTC holders, crew, transfer passengers, persons aged 17 and under or 65 and over
Temporary exemption for designated countries runs until 2026-12-31 (extension notice on k-eta.go.kr dated 2026-03-20; embassy notices dated Dec 2025)
description: Electronic travel authorization required in principle for nationals of visa-free entry countries before boarding a flight or ship to Korea. Apply at www.k-eta.go.kr; review generally within 72 hours. Fee 10,000 KRW; valid 3 years (for applications from 2023-07-03) with multiple entries. A temporary exemption for designated countries (22 countries per portal notices; USA and Canada explicitly confirmed) is in effect until 2026-12-31; exempt nationals may still apply voluntarily to skip the paper/electronic arrival card.
policy_name: K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization)

conditions: Required for e-visa: passport copy, color photo 3.5x4.5cm, credit card for electronic fee payment, category-specific documents
description: The Korea Visa Portal (visa.go.kr) issues electronic visas only for specific categories: E-1/E-3/E-4/E-5/E-7 professional work (and F-3 dependents), C-3-3 medical tourism via certified institutions, C-3-4 short-term business with prior entry history, C-4 short-term employment for invited scientists, and D-2 study categories. General tourism (C-3-1) is not an e-visa category; tourists who need a visa must apply through a Korean embassy or consulate.
policy_name: Korea e-Visa (전자사증) — limited categories, no general tourist e-visa

conditions: Group of 3+ recruited by designated travel agencies; passenger lists submitted in advance replace individual arrival cards
Agency designation revoked if quarterly average absconding rate is 2% or more
Stay up to 15 days, nationwide (Jeju separately 30 days under existing regime)
description: Chinese group tourists (3 or more persons) recruited by designated travel agencies (Korean MCST-designated domestic agencies and Korean-mission-designated agencies in China) may enter Korea visa-free and travel nationwide for up to 15 days. Officially published period: 2025-09-29 to 2026-06-30. Separately, Chinese tourists are permitted 30 days visa-free for Jeju (individual and group). Whether the nationwide group program was extended past 2026-06-30 (media reported extension to 2026-12-31) was NOT verified from a fetched official page.
policy_name: Temporary visa-free entry for Chinese group tourists (중국 단체관광객 한시 무사증)

conditions: Apply at the Korean mission with jurisdiction over the applicant's residence
Typical processing 4-7 working days (Embassy in UAE); longer if interview/investigation needed
Financial documents (e.g., 3 months of bank statements) commonly required for tourist applications
description: Nationals not covered by visa waiver agreements or designated visa-free entry must obtain a visa from a Korean embassy or consulate before travel. The relevant tourist category is short-term visit C-3 (e.g., C-3-9 general tourist), for stays of 90 days or less. Standard government fee schedule: single entry up to 90 days USD 40; single entry 91+ days USD 60; double entry USD 70; multiple entry USD 90 (charged in local-currency equivalents that vary by post and by nationality-specific reciprocity arrangements, e.g., 160/280/360 AED at the Embassy in the UAE). Issuance is discretionary; documents do not guarantee a visa.
policy_name: Short-term visit visa (C-3) via Korean embassies and consulates

conditions: 'ZAIRE' appears on the official list but conflicts with 'Democratic Republic of Congo' on the visa-required list; excluded from the ISO mapping
description: Official Immigration Department list of 51 countries whose nationals do not require a visa to enter Malaysia. The page does not publish maximum-stay durations for this list; period of stay is granted as a Social Visit Pass at entry.
policy_name: Countries that do not require a visa to enter Malaysia

conditions: Myanmar nationals are excluded and require a visa
Timor-Leste not addressed on the fetched page
description: Visa is not required for a stay of less than one (1) month for ASEAN nationals except Myanmar. Visas are required where the duration of stay exceeds one (1) month, except for Brunei and Singapore nationals.
policy_name: ASEAN visa-free entry

conditions: Maximum stay under the exemption not stated on the fetched official page
description: Official page states verbatim: "India** citizen: visa exempts until 31st December 2026". India otherwise sits on the visa-required list.
policy_name: Temporary visa exemption for Indian citizens

conditions: Per-entry and cumulative stay limits not verified from a fetched official Malaysian page
description: The Immigration Department publishes an FAQ page titled 'FAQ Malaysia – China Mutual Visa Exemption', and China is absent from the official visa-required country list, confirming a mutual visa exemption regime for Chinese nationals. Stay limits and effective dates could not be verified because the FAQ body is client-rendered.
policy_name: Malaysia-China mutual visa exemption

conditions: Eligible nationalities not verified from a fetchable official page
description: Online visa application facility operated by the Immigration Department of Malaysia. The department's official notice states: "For official Malaysia eVISA applications, visit the website : https://malaysiavisa.imi.gov.my". The portal's eligible-nationality list, fees and stay durations are rendered client-side and could not be verified in this pass.
policy_name: Malaysia eVISA (MYVISA)

conditions: Proof of sufficient funds for staying in Malaysia
Valid and confirmed return ticket
description: Single Entry Visa: for foreign nationals requiring a visa, mainly for a social visit; normally valid for a single entry within three (3) months of issue. Multiple Entry Visa: mainly business/government-to-government, valid three (3) to twelve (12) months; citizens of India and China may obtain it for social visits (1-year validity, 30 days per entry, no extension; RM100.00 for Indian citizens, RM30.00 for PRC citizens). Transit Visa for transit passengers leaving the airside area.
policy_name: Single Entry Visa / Multiple Entry Visa / Transit Visa

conditions: Hong Kong SAR: 'Hong Kong Special Administrative Region' passport holders only
Macao SAR: 'Regiao Administrativa Especial de Macau' passport holders only
Taiwan: passports including an identity card number only
Kosovo: biometric passports issued in line with ICAO standards only
Georgia, Moldova, Ukraine: biometric passports issued in line with ICAO standards only
North Macedonia, Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro: biometric passports only

Several states (e.g. United Arab Emirates, Dominica, Micronesia, Grenada, Kiribati, Saint Lucia, and footnote-3 states such as Peru, Palau, Marshall Islands, Nauru, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Tuvalu, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines): exemption applies from entry into force of a visa-exemption agreement with the European Union
Entry subject to Schengen Borders Code conditions, including proof of sufficient financial means (2026: 122 EUR per person per day, minimum 1,099 EUR for stays of 9 days or more)
description: Nationals of Annex II states, the Chinese SARs and listed entities are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area, for tourism among other non-gainful purposes. Published by the Spanish MFA (Washington consulate) as 'Lista paises obligados y exentos de visado Schengen 2025'. Also exempt: British nationals who are not British citizens (BN(O), BOTC, BOC, BPP, BS) under Annex II Part 3.
policy_name: Schengen visa-exemption list applied by Spain (Annex II, Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, consolidated 03.02.2025)

conditions: Application in person by appointment only
Apply in country of residence or origin

Passport valid at least 90 days (3 months) beyond expected departure from the Schengen area, issued within the previous 10 years, with at least two blank visa pages (application requirement at Washington consulate)
description: Nationals listed in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 need a Schengen visa to travel to Spain for tourism. Applications are lodged in person, by appointment, at the Spanish consulate competent for the applicant's residence or at its authorized BLS Spain Visa Application Center. The visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period in the Schengen area for tourism, business, family visits, medical treatment, studies, non-work internships or volunteer activities.
policy_name: Schengen short-stay (type C) visa via Spanish consulates and BLS visa application centers

conditions: Not yet operational; no application possible or required as of the snapshot date
Will apply to visa-exempt (Annex II) nationals when it starts
description: EU travel authorization that will apply to visa-exempt third-country nationals travelling to Spain and the other participating European countries. Not in operation as of 2026-07-23: the Spanish MFA states it 'is expected to become operational in the last quarter of 2026'; spain.info states it 'will be mandatory from the last quarter of 2026' and cites a 20 EUR fee, multiple entries, 90 days per 180-day period.
policy_name: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) - announced, not yet operational

conditions: National identity document or valid passport accepted
description: Citizens of the European Union, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland may enter and travel within Spain with their national identity document or valid passport; no visa and no 90/180 visa-policy cap.
policy_name: EU/EEA/Swiss freedom of movement

conditions: Applies to third-country nationals crossing Schengen external borders
description: Since October 2025, travellers from non-EU/non-Schengen countries must register with the Entry/Exit System when arriving in or leaving Spain. Not a visa; border-registration requirement.
policy_name: EU Entry/Exit System (EES) biometric registration

conditions: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine: biometric passports required
Taiwan: only holders of passports that include an identity card number
Serbia: passports issued by the Serbian Coordination Directorate excluded
San Marino and Holy See nationals are always exempt
description: Official MAECI (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation) list of nationalities exempt from the short-stay visa requirement for stays of up to 90 days within a 180-day period, for tourism, missions, business, invitations, religious reasons, transit, transport, sport competitions and study.
policy_name: Countries whose nationals are exempt from the requirement of short-stay visas

conditions: Apply no more than 6 months and no later than 15 days before intended travel
Applicants must apply in person at the competent mission for their place of legal residence
Decisions on C visas are generally reached within 15 calendar days (up to 15 working days cited by Embassy Dublin)
description: Nationalities not on the exemption list must obtain a Schengen type-C visa before travel for tourist stays up to 90 days in any 180-day period. The official MAECI portal 'Il visto per l'Italia' determines the requirement via a guided questionnaire and provides forms; applications are lodged in person with the Italian embassy/consulate holding jurisdiction over the applicant's residence, or at a visa application center mandated by that mission. Many missions require appointments via the official Prenot@mi portal.
policy_name: Schengen short-stay visa (type C) for tourism

conditions: Applies to third-country nationals (both visa-exempt and visa holders) crossing Schengen external borders, including Italy's
description: Centralized EU system for the electronic registration of entry, exit and refusal of entry of third-country nationals crossing the external Schengen border, replacing manual passport stamping. It is a border registration system, not a visa or travel authorisation.
policy_name: EU Entry/Exit System (EES)

conditions: The authoritative list is published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (mfaic.gov.kh, list page dated 2025-03-26), which was unreachable (WAF 'Request Rejected'); the list here is taken from the Royal Embassy of Cambodia in London FAQ and may lag MFAIC updates
description: Bilateral and ASEAN visa exemption agreements. Ordinary/regular-passport exemptions for tourism: Brunei 14 days, Indonesia 30, Lao PDR 30, Malaysia 30, Myanmar 14, Philippines 30, Singapore 30, Thailand 14, Vietnam 30, Hong Kong SAR 30, Hungary 15. All other countries on the list (e.g. China, India, Japan, South Korea, Russia, Brazil, Kuwait, Turkey, Iran, Mongolia, Belarus, Seychelles) are exempt for diplomatic/official passports only.
policy_name: List of Visa Exemption between Cambodia and other Countries

conditions: Government fee could not be verified from an official page (portal unreachable to our fetcher); widely reported as USD 30 for tourist e-Visa since 2025-01-01 - unverified
Per-nationality eligibility restrictions could not be verified
description: Online tourist visa issued via the official portal https://www.evisa.gov.kh, operated by the E-Visa Office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation. Tourist (T) class: single entry, valid to enter within 3 months of issue, 30-day stay. Accepted at a published list of ports of entry.
policy_name: Cambodia e-Visa (Tourist Type-T)

conditions: Fee (widely reported USD 30 tourist / USD 35 business) not verified on an official page
Per-nationality eligibility restrictions not verified
description: Visas on arrival are available for tourists at major international entry checkpoints (including Bavet, Poipet and Cham Yeam land borders) per the Royal Embassy of Cambodia in London FAQ. Fee and eligibility details are not stated on any fetched official page.
policy_name: Cambodia visa on arrival

conditions: Passport valid at least 6 months at date of entry; blank-page requirement varies by embassy (DC: at least 1 blank visa page; London/Canberra: at least 2 blank pages)
description: Standard tourist visa issued by Cambodian embassies and consulates: single entry, valid to enter Cambodia within 3 months of issue, 30-day allowable stay, extendable once for another 30 days at the Cambodia Immigration Office. Fee at the Washington DC embassy: USD 30. Issued visas are not refundable or transferable.
policy_name: Tourist (Type-T / T Class) consular visa

conditions: Free of charge
Submit within 7 days before or on arrival
description: All travelers must submit the Cambodia e-Arrival card, available at https://arrival.gov.kh, within 7 days before or on arrival. Submission is free. Operated under the General Department of Immigration.
policy_name: Cambodia e-Arrival card (CeA)

conditions: Machine-readable electronic passport (e-Passport)
Approved ESTA before travel (air, sea, and land)
Stay of 90 days or less for business or pleasure
Round-trip ticket unless exempted
No presence in Iraq, Syria, state sponsors of terrorism, or designated countries/areas of concern on/after 2011-03-01 (exemptions/waivers possible)
Waiver of right to review or appeal admissibility decisions (other than asylum)
UK designation limited to British citizens with right of permanent abode; Taiwan limited to e-passports with household registration number
description: Citizens/nationals of designated countries may be admitted at U.S. ports of entry as nonimmigrant visitors for business or pleasure for 90 days or less without a visa, subject to eligibility conditions (e-passport, approved ESTA, round-trip ticket, travel-history restrictions for Iraq/Syria/state sponsors of terrorism since 2011-03-01, etc.). List per 8 CFR 217.2 as amended by the Qatar designation (89 FR 78783); Romania was subsequently removed from the approved list (CBP notice, 90 FR 57208, Dec 10, 2025). DHS maintains the current list at https://www.dhs.gov/visa-waiver-program (page not directly fetchable).
policy_name: Visa Waiver Program (VWP)

conditions: Required for every VWP traveler prior to travel
e-Passport required
ESTA validity: generally 2 years, multiple entries
Official application portal: https://esta.cbp.dhs.gov/
description: Mandatory online travel authorization for all Visa Waiver Program travelers arriving by air, sea, or land. Approval is generally valid for two years (or until passport expiry) and allows multiple visits. FY2026 fee USD 40.27 (USD 10.27 retained if the application is denied), assessed from January 1, 2026 under HR-1 (Public Law 119-21). Applications processed up to 72 hours. CBP has proposed making the ESTA Mobile application the sole application platform.
policy_name: Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA)

conditions: Form DS-160 application
Interview at a U.S. embassy or consulate
USD 185 application processing fee (22 CFR 22.1, Item 21)
Additional visa issuance (reciprocity) fee may apply for some nationalities (not verified)
description: Default channel for all nationalities not covered by the VWP or a specific exemption: apply to the Department of State with Form DS-160, attend an interview at a U.S. embassy or consulate, pay the USD 185 non-petition-based nonimmigrant visa application processing fee. Renewals must also be done at a U.S. embassy or consulate. Period of admission is determined by CBP at entry (B-2 admission period not verified from a fetched official source).
policy_name: B-2 visitor visa (tourism)

conditions: Exceptions for E, K, S, V nonimmigrant categories (visa required)
Passport or approved WHTI-compliant document required
BCC facility applies to Mexican nationals at land ports of entry from Mexico
description: Under 8 CFR 212.1, a visa is generally not required for Canadian citizens or citizens of the British Overseas Territory of Bermuda (exceptions: E, K, S, V categories). Passport required, with alternative WHTI-compliant documents (NEXUS, FAST, SENTRI, INAC card; birth certificate options for Canadian children at land/sea ports). Mexican nationals with a biometric B-1/B-2 Border Crossing Card (DSP-150) may enter from Mexico at land ports without a separate visa/passport.
policy_name: Canada and Bermuda visa exemption / Western Hemisphere Travel Initiative (WHTI)

conditions: Applies to PRC-passport holders with 10-year B-1/B-2 category visas
Enrollment fee paid at time of enrollment
description: Nationals of the People's Republic of China holding 10-year B-1, B-2, or B-1/B-2 visitor visas must enroll in EVUS and keep their information current to receive a determination of travel eligibility before traveling to the United States (8 CFR part 215, subpart B). FY2026 enrollment fee USD 30.75, assessed from January 1, 2026.
policy_name: Electronic Visa Update System (EVUS)

conditions: Valid only for entry to Guam or CNMI, not the U.S. mainland
Form I-736 required (transition to mandatory electronic submission proposed)
PRC parole facility: CNMI only, up to 14 days
description: Public Law 110-229 exempts certain nationalities from the nonimmigrant visa requirement for visits of up to 45 days limited to Guam or the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI). At the Secretary's discretion, PRC passport holders without a visitor visa may be allowed to enter the CNMI only for up to 14 days under discretionary parole. The list of eligible countries for this territorial program was not verified from a fetched official source.
maximum_stay: 45 days (Guam/CNMI); 14 days for PRC nationals paroled into CNMI
policy_name: Guam-CNMI Visa Waiver Program (Form I-736)

conditions: No gainful employment during the visa-free stay
Biometric-passport-only conditions for ALB, BIH, GEO, XKX, MDA, MNE, MKD, SRB, UKR
SAR-passport-only conditions for HKG and MAC; identity-card-number condition for TWN
MUS and SYC: 3 months within 6 months instead of 90/180
description: Official Austrian Ministry of the Interior list of nationalities exempt from the EU short-stay visa requirement (regular 90 days within 180 days). 63 countries/territories carry EU-Visumpflicht 'Nein'. Conditions apply for some: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Ukraine, Kosovo (biometric passports only); Georgia (biometric ordinary passports only); Hong Kong ('Hong Kong Special Administrative Region' passport only); Macao (Regiao Administrativa Especial de Macau passport only); Taiwan (passports with identity card number only); Mauritius and Seychelles (3 months within 6 months).
policy_name: Visapflichten und Visabefreiungen fuer die Einreise in die EU+Oesterreich (BMI, Stand 15.7.2026) — EU-Visumbefreiung

conditions: Right of entry and residence under EU free-movement law; not subject to the 90/180-day short-stay limit
description: Citizens of EU member states, EEA states (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) and Switzerland do not need a visa for entering Austria; the BMI list marks all three visa columns 'EU-Freizuegigkeit' for these 30 countries.
policy_name: EU-Freizuegigkeit (EU/EEA/Swiss freedom of movement)

conditions: Personal appearance and appointment required (also for children)
Passport not older than 10 years, valid for three months after expiry of the visa, with two free pages
description: Nationals not exempt by EU regulation need a Schengen visa C for tourism (max 90 days per 180 days), applied for in person at the competent Austrian Consulate in the country of legal residence; several consulates have outsourced lodgement to the external service provider VFS (e.g. India, UAE). Applications no earlier than 6 months and no later than 15 days before departure; standard processing up to 15 calendar days.
policy_name: Schengen visa C (tourist/visit) via Austrian representations abroad

conditions: Will apply to visa-exempt third-country nationals once operational; expected start Q4/2026
description: Per the Austrian Ministry of the Interior, ETIAS is 'derzeit noch nicht in Betrieb' (currently not yet in operation). Visa-exempt third-country nationals are expected to need an ETIAS travel authorisation for Schengen entry from approximately Q4/2026; fee EUR 7 (some travelers exempt); application via the official EU ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu) or mobile app. Not a requirement at the snapshot date 2026-07-23.
policy_name: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) — NOT yet in operation

conditions: Applies to the stay in Austria under the respective bilateral agreement; see BMI list per-country entries
description: In addition to the EU 90/180 exemption, Austria's BMI list records national (bilateral) visa exemptions for stays in Austria for some countries, flagged 'EES-Sonderregelung Altabkommen': e.g. Japan 6 months (all categories); Australia, Canada, Singapore 3 months (all categories); South Korea ordinary passports 90 days (diplomatic/service 180 days); Brazil ordinary passports 3 months.
policy_name: Nationale Visumbefreiung (Oesterreich) — bilateral national visa exemptions (EES-Sonderregelung Altabkommen)

conditions: Maximum stay 90 days in any 180-day period for visa-exempt third-country nationals
Travel document valid at least three months after intended departure from the Schengen area and issued within the last 10 years
Exemption does not cover gainful occupation for V1-marked nationalities (visa required for listed work sectors or any employment exceeding 8 days per calendar year)
description: Switzerland's authoritative nationality-by-nationality list of ID and visa provisions, published by the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM). Nationalities marked 'No' for stays up to 90 days enter visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Footnotes: V1 (visa still required for certain gainful occupation), V2 (British Citizen exemption), V12/V13/V18 (biometric passports only), V14 (Taiwan passport must contain identity card number), V16/V17 (Hong Kong/Macao SAR passports). Complete exempt set recorded in applies_to_nationalities.
policy_name: Overview of ID and visa provisions according to nationality (Annex CH-1, List 1)

conditions: Must present valid personal identification, an ID card or a passport
Must not pose a threat to public order and security
description: Citizens of EU and EFTA states do not require a visa to enter Switzerland; they enter with a valid ID card or passport under the free-movement rules and need only a registration/residence permit for stays exceeding 90 days.
policy_name: EU/EFTA free movement entry

conditions: Demonstrate purpose and circumstances of the stay
Demonstrate sufficient financial means for the stay and the return
Travel document issued less than ten years ago and valid at least three months after intended departure from the Schengen area
Not listed in the Schengen Information System (SIS) for refusal of entry; no threat to public order, internal security or public health
description: Visa-required nationalities must obtain a Schengen visa type C for tourist stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. The SEM does not issue visas; Swiss representations abroad issue or refuse them. Applications are submitted online via the official swiss-visa.ch online visa system or directly to the competent Swiss representation. Fee EUR 90 (adults) / EUR 45 (children 6-12).
policy_name: Schengen visa type C (short stay, incl. tourism)

conditions: Not yet in operation as of 2026-07-23
description: SEM states that ETIAS, a new European travel authorisation system that will cover visa-exempt travellers to the Schengen area including Switzerland, launches in the final quarter of 2026, will cost 20 euros and will generally be valid for 3 years. As of the snapshot date 2026-07-23 it is not in operation and no travel authorisation is required.
policy_name: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) - announced, not yet in operation

conditions: Short-term non-profit stays only; employment requires a Schengen visa for employment
90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area; stay cannot be extended
Registration with the Foreign Police within 3 working days of arrival
description: Czech MFA list of states and territories whose citizens may enter the Czech Republic (Schengen Area) visa-free for short-term non-profit stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Includes conditional exemptions: biometric passports required for Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine; Taiwan passports must contain an identity card number; Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passports only; five categories of British nationals also exempt.
policy_name: List of States Whose Citizens Are Exempt from Visa Requirement (Schengen short-stay)

conditions: Additional stay valid in the Czech Republic only; no travel to other Schengen states
Argentina, Chile, Israel, South Korea, Costa Rica, Malaysia, Uruguay: additional 90 days; Singapore: additional 30 days
description: Under bilateral agreements, citizens of Argentina, Chile, Israel, South Korea, Costa Rica, Malaysia and Uruguay may stay in the Czech Republic an additional 90 days beyond the Schengen 90/180 allowance, and citizens of Singapore an additional 30 days. The bilateral stay applies only within the Czech Republic, with no travel to other EU/Schengen states during it.
maximum_stay: Up to 90 additional days in the Czech Republic (30 for Singapore) after the Schengen 90/180 allowance
policy_name: Bilateral visa-waiver agreements extending stay in the Czech Republic

conditions: Apply in country of citizenship or residence within the applicant's consular district
Adult fee EUR 90; children 6-11 EUR 45; under 6 free; fee not refunded on refusal
For multi-country Schengen travel, apply with the state that is the only or main destination or of longest stay
description: Third-country nationals not on the visa-exemption list must obtain a Schengen short-term visa (Type C) for tourist stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Applications are filed at Czech consulates or outsourced visa centers in the applicant's consular district, commonly in person, not at a border crossing nor inside the Czech Republic; in some countries another Schengen state represents Czechia for visa issuance.
policy_name: Schengen short-term visa (Type C) for tourism

conditions: Not yet in force as of 2026-07-23; scheduled for the last quarter of 2026
Official EU application site: https://travel-europe.europa.eu/etias_en
description: The EU-wide ETIAS travel authorization will apply to citizens of over 60 visa-exempt countries traveling to the Czech Republic and other Schengen states. Czech embassy pages state it starts in the last quarter of 2026; as of the 2026-07-23 snapshot date it is NOT yet in operation and no ETIAS is required.
policy_name: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorization System) - announced, not yet operational

conditions: Stay limited to 90 days in any 180-day period
No employment
Passport annotations per official list (SAR passports for HKG/MAC; identity card number for TWN)
description: The Federal Foreign Office publishes an overview of visa requirements/exemptions for entry into Germany. Nationals of the countries marked 'no' may enter visa-free for short stays (tourism included) of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Annotations apply to some passports (Hong Kong/Macao SAR passports; Taiwan passports with identity card number; Georgia official passports require a visa).
policy_name: German/Schengen short-stay visa exemption list (Staatenliste zur Visumpflicht)

conditions: Apply in person at the competent German mission or its visa application centre
Application possible at the earliest 6 months and generally no later than 15 days before the trip
Proof of purpose, sufficient funds and return trip financing may be required
description: Third-country nationals not on the exemption list must obtain a Schengen visa (type C) before travel, applied for at the German embassy/consulate covering their place of residence, or at a mandated external visa application centre (e.g. VFS Global in India, where missions no longer accept Schengen applications directly). The visa entitles the holder to visits of up to 90 days every 6 months in the entire Schengen area. Standard processing time is up to 15 calendar days.
maximum_stay: 90 days every 6 months in the entire Schengen area
policy_name: Schengen visa (type C) via German missions abroad

conditions: Will apply only to visa-exempt third-country nationals once operational
Not yet required for travel as of 2026-07-23
description: EU-level travel authorisation that will apply to visa-exempt travellers visiting 30 European countries (including Germany as a Schengen state) for short stays up to 90 days in any 180-day period. As of 2026-07-23 ETIAS "is currently not in operation and no applications for travel authorisations are collected at this point"; the launch date will be announced several months in advance. Fee will be EUR 20.
policy_name: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) — planned, not yet operational

conditions: Valid national passport or identity card
description: EU nationals (and EEA/Swiss nationals) are exempt from the visa requirement for entry into Germany; the Federal Foreign Office states an exemption from the third-country visa requirement applies to EU nationals.
policy_name: EU/EEA/Swiss freedom of movement

conditions: Stay limited to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area
Complete nationality list not retrievable from reachable official pages; verify per nationality via the official France-Visas Visa wizard (france-visas.gouv.fr)
description: France applies the common Schengen short-stay visa policy. Per the MEAE, 59 nationalities are exempt from the short-stay visa for stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period ('Depending on your nationality and the type of your passport, you may be exempt from a visa'). The complete official list is served by the France-Visas 'Visa wizard', which was inaccessible to automated retrieval (HTTP 403); only USA membership was individually verified from an official French page. Visa-exempt travelers are subject to EES biometric registration at the external border and, from ETIAS go-live (expected Q4 2026), will need an ETIAS travel authorization.
policy_name: Schengen short-stay visa waiver (59 visa-exempt nationalities)

conditions: Applies to all EU, EEA and Swiss citizens (DEU and FRA listed here as the requested nationalities covered)
Valid passport or national identity card required for identity checks
description: European citizens can enter and be present for up to 3 months in France without special formalities, needing only a valid passport or identity document; no residence permit or work authorization is required. They are excluded from EES registration.
maximum_stay: 3 months without formalities; longer under free-movement rules
policy_name: EU/EEA/Swiss free movement

conditions: Metropolitan France only
Must be invoked at border crossing into France
No paid work for a French employer, long-term study, or taking up residence
description: U.S. citizens may spend 90 days in metropolitan France without a visa regardless of previous Schengen stays, in addition to the standard 90-day Schengen visa exception. The bilateral-agreement stay must take place after the Schengen visa-exception stay, and the traveler must state the desire to invoke the agreement at the French border so the EES file is manually updated. Tourism/short visits only.
maximum_stay: 90 days under Schengen exception + 90 days in metropolitan France under the bilateral agreement
policy_name: France-USA bilateral agreement of 1 April 1949

conditions: Passport valid at least 3 months after the visa end date, issued within the last 10 years, at least 2 blank pages
Visa fee payable at lodging; amount published in the France-Visas 'Tarifs' section (not retrievable — see unresolved)
Statutory documents on purpose of stay, means of support and accommodation must be presentable at the border
description: Non-exempt nationalities must obtain a Schengen short-stay visa before travel. The application is completed online on the official France-Visas portal, then submitted in person to the applicant's local visa centre or the French consulate in the country of residence; the portal also handles tracking. Applications may be lodged up to six months before departure. The visa allows up to 90 days (continuous or cumulative) in the Schengen Area per 180-day period.
policy_name: Schengen short-stay (uniform) visa via France-Visas and local visa centre

conditions: Not in force as of 2026-07-23
Will apply only to visa-exempt (59-country list) short-stay travelers once live
description: ETIAS is a travel authorization distinct from a visa, comparable to the USA's ESTA or the UK's ETA. It will apply to nationals of the 59 visa-exempt countries entering the Schengen zone. Fee EUR 20 (waived for under-18s, over-70s and certain family members); valid for multiple entries over 3 years; maximum stay 90 days per 180-day period. As of the retrieval date it is not operational: 'Expected to come on line in the last quarter of 2026' and 'No websites currently issue ETIAS travel authorizations.' Official EU resource: travel-europe.europa.eu.
policy_name: ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorisation System) — not yet in force

conditions: Not a visa or authorization — a border registration system
Applies at the external borders of the 29 Schengen Area countries
description: EES is a European database in which Member States record the data of nationals of non-EU and non-Schengen Area countries who cross the external borders. It applies to all third-country nationals entering for short stays (max 90 days per 180-day period), whether visa-required or visa-exempt, and replaces passport stamping. Biometric data collected: facial image and, for travelers 12+, fingerprints. Gradual implementation began 12 October 2025; fully operational since 10 April 2026. Registration is free. EU/Schengen citizens and nationals of Andorra, San Marino, Monaco and the Holy See are excluded.
policy_name: EES (Entry/Exit System) border registration

conditions: Biometric passport required for Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine
Taiwan passports must include an identity card number
Hong Kong and Macao exemptions apply to SAR passports
description: Portugal's MFA visa portal publishes the list of nationalities exempt from the short-stay (Schengen) visa requirement, including special provisions for Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passports, Taiwan passports containing an identity card number, and biometric-passport-only exemptions for certain Western Balkan and Eastern Partnership countries.
policy_name: List of nationalities exempt from holding a visa (short stay / Schengen)

conditions: Travel medical insurance covering the entire stay required
Proof of means of subsistence (e.g. last three bank statements), return travel reservation, and accommodation proof (hotel reservation or statement of responsibility) required
description: Nationalities not on the exemption list must obtain a Schengen short-stay visa (up to 90 days in each 180-day period; tourism among the covered purposes; single or multiple entry) before travel. Applications are lodged at the Portuguese embassy/consulate designated for the applicant's country of residence, via external service providers (VFS Global, TLS Contact, BLS International) where designated, or online through the MFA E-Visa platform; in some countries another EU member state's embassy processes applications in representation of Portugal.
policy_name: Schengen short-stay visa (tourism) via the Portuguese consular network

conditions: Derived from the official MFA Schengen-area membership list; the page does not itself elaborate free-movement rules
description: Portugal is a Schengen area member. Nationals of the other Schengen/EU member states listed on the official MFA page (including Germany and France) are not subject to Portugal's short-stay visa regime.
policy_name: Schengen area membership / EU free movement

conditions: Tourism only
Apply at least 7 days before departure
Passport valid at least 6 months from arrival date
Entry may be refused by port authorities despite visa approval
description: Official Electronic Visa Portal for touristic visits for selected countries at www.visa2egypt.gov.eg. Tourist visa only; single-entry USD 30 or multiple-entry USD 65, paid online by credit/debit card. Application must be created at least 7 days before departure. Port authorities retain the right to refuse entry.
maximum_stay: 30 days (single entry, per consular description of Egyptian tourist visas); not explicitly stated on the portal pages fetched
policy_name: Egypt e-Visa (tourism)

conditions: Fee USD 25 or equivalent in Egyptian pounds payable on arrival
Nationalities requiring pre-approval cannot acquire visa upon arrival
description: Nationals of listed countries can obtain a visa upon arrival at any Egyptian port of entry for USD 25 (or equivalent in Egyptian pounds). Single-entry tourist visas allow a maximum stay of 30 days.
policy_name: Egypt tourist visa on arrival

conditions: Passport valid at least 6 months
Pre-approval nationalities cannot use visa on arrival
Consular fees vary by post (e.g. USD 32/67 at Washington DC; GBP 33/68 at London)
description: All nationalities not covered by the eVisa or visa-on-arrival channels must obtain a visa in advance from an Egyptian embassy or consulate. Single Entry Visas are valid for 6 months and allow a maximum stay of ONLY 30 days; Multiple Entry Visas are valid for 6 months and allow a collective stay of 90 days. Nationals of Afghanistan, Ethiopia, Iran, Israel, Mali, Niger, Palestine, Sudan, Syria and holders of any travel document require security pre-approval (6-8 weeks minimum, up to 3 months).
policy_name: Egyptian consular tourist visa (default channel)

conditions: Valid only for the Sharm El Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba and Taba resort areas; travel beyond them requires a visa
description: Nationals of the UK, EU members, and the USA travelling to Sharm El Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba and Taba resorts ONLY, for a maximum of 15 DAYS (consulate FAQ states 14 days), do not require a visa prior to travelling; a FREE entry permission stamp is granted upon arrival.
policy_name: Sinai resorts free entry permission stamp

conditions: Maximum stay 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area
Passport valid at least 3 months after intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years
Biometric passport required for ordinary-passport holders of Kosovo, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia and Ukraine
Taiwan passports must include an identity card number; Hong Kong/Macao must hold SAR passports
description: Nationals of third countries listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 are exempt from the visa requirement for stays not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period. EU/EEA citizens enter freely with passport or national ID card. Special conditions: Hong Kong and Macao SAR passports qualify; Taiwan passports must contain an identity card number; ordinary-passport holders of Kosovo, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia and Ukraine need biometric passports; Serbian passports issued by the Serbian Coordination Directorate are excluded; several British national categories (BNO, BOTC, BOC, BPP, BS) are also exempt.
policy_name: Visa exemption under Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 Annex II (Schengen short-stay)

conditions: In-person submission at the competent Hungarian consulate or its mandated visa application center
Application window: 6 months to 15 days before travel
Decision within 15 calendar days, extendable to 45 days
A visa is a preliminary permission for entry, not an automatic entry authorization
description: Non-exempt nationals must obtain a Schengen C visa before travel, applied for in person at the Hungarian consulate covering their habitual residence; in several jurisdictions applications are lodged through visa application centers operated by VFS Global. Applications may be filed 6 months to 15 days before the intended visit; decisions within 15 calendar days (extendable to 45). The visa is valid for the whole Schengen Area. Tourist supporting documents: travel-agency certificate or prepaid accommodation reservation.
policy_name: Schengen short-stay (C) visa via Hungarian consulates

conditions: Generally ordinary passport holders; some entries cover official passports too; touristic purposes
Durations vary by nationality: typically 90 days (often within any 180-day period); Russia 60 days; Belarus/Indonesia/Thailand 30 days per entry per the MFA page
Kosovo also appears on the MFA page but has no standard ISO alpha-3 code and is omitted from the list above
description: The MFA 'Visa Information For Foreigners' page lists, country by country, which passport holders are exempt from visa and for how long. Most exempt nationalities get 90 days (many explicitly '90 days in any 180-day period'); some have shorter limits (e.g. Russia 60 days; Belarus, Indonesia and Thailand 30 days per entry per the same page). China (ordinary passports) was added as of 2 January 2026. The 16 pipeline target nationalities were verified verbatim; the broader membership below reflects the fetched page but was not individually verbatim-verified for duration.
maximum_stay: typically 90 days in any 180-day period (30 or 60 days for some nationalities)
policy_name: Türkiye visa exemptions for touristic travel (MFA country-by-country list)

conditions: Tourism or commerce only; other purposes require a consular visa
List also covers 'Hong Kong (BN(O))' British National (Overseas) passports (no distinct ISO code; not included in the code list above)
Croatia, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania appear on the eligible list although the MFA lists them as visa-exempt for ordinary passports
description: Official e-Visa launched 17 April 2013 by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, applied for online at www.evisa.gov.tr. Valid only for tourism or commerce. 48 nationalities/travel documents are eligible 'provided that they meet required criteria'; per-country criteria, fee and validity are displayed inside the application flow. Conditional nationalities must hold a valid Schengen/USA/UK/Ireland visa or residence permit, a return ticket, hotel reservation and at least 50 USD per day, and enter via airports (not valid at land border checkpoints).
policy_name: Republic of Türkiye Electronic Visa (e-Visa) Application System

conditions: Fee table dated 10 November 2014, 'as of 1 May 2014'; most listed nationalities have since become visa-exempt
Hong Kong BN(O) passports also listed (no distinct ISO code)
description: The MFA visa information page states that fees for e-Visas obtained via www.evisa.gov.tr are lower than fees for visas obtained upon arrival to Turkish airports, and the MFA fee schedule PDF (dated 10 November 2014) lists visa-on-arrival fees at Turkish airports for 38 nationalities. The schedule predates later exemptions (e.g. USA, Canada, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Oman, China), so the current practical scope of visa on arrival could not be confirmed on a current-dated official page.
policy_name: Visa on arrival at Turkish airports (fee schedule as of 1 May 2014)

conditions: Default channel for nationalities that are neither visa-exempt nor able to use the e-Visa, and for purposes other than tourism/commerce
description: Since 5 January 2016 all Turkish sticker (consular) visa applications must be made through the Pre-Application System (www.visa.gov.tr; pre-application and appointments also via www.konsolosluk.gov.tr). Applicants upload data online (or via a visa application center), then submit signed forms and passports at the Turkish Mission or, where designated, at an authorized visa application center (e.g. Anatolia Visa Application Centers, sole authorized provider for Turkish missions in Pakistan since 1 May 2021). Where internet is weak, applications can still be made directly at Turkish Missions. Work and study visas are issued by Turkish Embassies or Consulates.
policy_name: Turkish sticker visa via Pre-Application System

conditions: Passport valid at least 6 months from date of arrival
China and reciprocal-exemption countries: ordinary passports only
description: GCC nationals enter with passport or national ID, no visa. Listed EU & associated nations receive up to 90 days within any 180-day period. A separate list of nations receives a 30-day visa-free entry. A reciprocal exemption (ordinary passports) grants 30 days to Seychelles, Bahamas, Argentina, and China. All require passports valid at least 6 months.
maximum_stay: 90 days (EU/associated group) or 30 days (other exempt/reciprocal groups)
policy_name: UAE visa-free entry - GCC and reciprocal/EU list

conditions: Holder of valid US visa/green card or UK/EU residence permit
Permit/visa valid at least 6 months from arrival
description: Indian citizens holding a valid U.S. visa, U.S. green card, UK residence permit, or EU residence permit can obtain an entry visa on arrival valid for 14 days for a fee of AED 100. (Indian ordinary passport holders are separately in the 30-day visa-free list.)
policy_name: Conditional visa on arrival for Indian passport holders

conditions: Applied online/through a sponsor (airline, hotel, agent, ICP smart services)
5-year multi-entry visa requires ~USD 4,000 bank balance over 6 months, 180-day UAE health insurance, and return/onward ticket
description: Nationals not eligible for visa-free entry must obtain a tourist entry permit before travel. Applications are made online through the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP), through GDRFA-Dubai, through UAE national airlines (Emirates, Etihad, flydubai), or through licensed travel agents and hotels. UAE embassies do not issue tourist visas. A 5-year multiple-entry tourist visa (90 days per visit, extendable 90 more) is also available with financial and insurance conditions.
maximum_stay: 30 or 60 days per single/multiple entry visit (5-year visa: 90 days per visit)
policy_name: UAE tourist visa (sponsor-based, online)

conditions: Maximum 90 days in any 180-day period
Some exemptions are limited to biometric-passport holders or subject to specific passport types (Hong Kong/Macao/Taiwan)
description: Nationals of third countries listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 are exempt from the short-stay visa requirement for the Schengen area, including Greece, for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. List includes (non-exhaustive): Andorra, United Arab Emirates, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Barbados, Brunei, Brazil, Bahamas, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Israel, Japan, Saint Kitts and Nevis, South Korea, Monaco, Mauritius, Mexico, Malaysia, New Zealand, Panama, Paraguay, Singapore, San Marino, El Salvador, Trinidad and Tobago, United States, Uruguay, Holy See, Venezuela, Samoa; plus Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passport holders, British citizens (via Reg 2019/592), and Taiwan passport holders whose passports include an identity-card number.
policy_name: Schengen short-stay visa exemption (Annex II, Regulation (EU) 2018/1806)

conditions: Apply at Greek consulate / authorised visa centre before travel
Adult fee EUR 90; reduced fees for children and certain nationalities
description: Nationals of countries listed in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 (e.g. China, India, Russia) must obtain a Schengen short-stay (type C) visa before travelling to Greece. Applications are submitted at the Greek consulate of the main destination or at an authorised visa-application centre. Standard adult fee EUR 90; passport must be valid at least three months beyond intended departure.
policy_name: Schengen short-stay (type C) visa

conditions: Standard exemption stay 90 days
Hong-Kong and Maldives: 30-day stay limit
Mali, Congo (Brazzaville), Guinea (Conakry): AEVM required despite exemption
description: Official consular list of nationalities exempt from an entry visa to Morocco. Standard exemption stay is 90 days; the list annotates only deviations (Hong-Kong and Maldives limited to 30 days). Mali, Congo (Brazzaville) and Guinea (Conakry) are listed but require an AEVM electronic travel authorization.
policy_name: List of countries whose citizens are exempted from entry visa into Morocco

conditions: Category A nationalities eligible by nationality
Category B: valid residence permit (>=180 days) in EU/USA/Australia/Canada/UK/Japan/Norway/New Zealand/UAE/Switzerland
Category C: multiple-entry non-electronic visa (>=90 days) from Schengen/USA/Australia/UK/Ireland/Japan/Canada/Norway/New Zealand
Ordinary passport valid >=90 days from application
Tourism or Business only; no residency
description: Online tourism/business eVisa issued to three categories of visa-subject foreigners: Category A (specific nationalities including India), Category B (residents of eligible countries holding a valid residence permit), Category C (holders of a multiple-entry visa from eligible countries). Single entry, max 30-day stay, eVisa valid 180 days from issue. Ordinary passports only. Express (24h) or Standard (72h) processing. Non-refundable.
policy_name: Morocco electronic visa (eVisa) - acces-maroc.ma

conditions: Requested online via www.acces-maroc.ma
Applies to specified visa-exempt nationalities
description: Electronic travel authorization required for certain visa-exempt nationalities before travel to Morocco, applied for online at www.acces-maroc.ma. The official consular exemption list flags Mali, Congo (Brazzaville) and Guinea (Conakry) as requiring an AEVM.
policy_name: Autorisation Electronique de Voyage au Maroc (AEVM)

conditions: Holders of diplomatic/service/special passports and travel documents for refugees/stateless persons must apply at an Embassy or Consulate General
description: Default channel for nationalities that are neither visa-exempt nor eVisa-eligible by nationality, and for holders of non-ordinary travel documents. Applications are lodged at the Moroccan Embassy or Consulate General near the applicant's place of residence.
policy_name: Consular tourist visa (Embassy / Consulate General of Morocco)

conditions: Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania: citizens only
Greece: passports issued on/after 1 January 2006 only
Hong Kong and Macau: specific passport type requirements apply
NZeTA required before travel; IVL of NZD 100 payable
description: Passport holders from listed visa waiver countries/territories do not need a Visitor Visa for a stay of less than 3 months (6 months for the United Kingdom), but must request an NZeTA before travel and pay the IVL. Australian citizens and permanent residents on an Australian passport need neither a visa nor an NZeTA.
maximum_stay: 3 months per visit (6 months for United Kingdom)
policy_name: New Zealand visa waiver countries and territories

conditions: Must be requested before travel; allow 72 hours
Cost from NZD 17 (app) / NZD 23 (website)
IVL of NZD 100 payable at the same time
You can only be in New Zealand for up to 6 months within any 12-month period
description: Electronic travel authority required for citizens of visa waiver countries/territories, cruise/cargo ship passengers, eligible travellers from Australia, and transit passengers. Allows visitor stays up to 3 months (6 months for UK) and transit up to 24 hours (Auckland International Airport only). Valid 2 years for travellers.
maximum_stay: 3 months per visit (6 months for United Kingdom); transit up to 24 hours
policy_name: New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority (NZeTA)

conditions: Government fee from NZD 441
IVL of NZD 100 payable
Passport valid at least 3 months after planned departure
description: Nationals not on the visa waiver list must apply for a Visitor Visa before travelling to New Zealand for tourism. Applications are made online through the Immigration New Zealand portal or by paper form INZ 1017.
policy_name: New Zealand Visitor Visa

conditions: Passport valid at least 3 months from date of arrival
Confirmed onward or return ticket
Compulsory health insurance from an MoPH-registered provider
Waiver is free of charge
Stay is 30 or 90 days depending on nationality; 30-day waiver extendable for another 30 days
description: Qatar grants visa-free entry (a free waiver issued on arrival) to citizens of around 100-102 nationalities for tourism. Stay is either 30 days or 90 days depending on nationality; the 30-day waiver is extendable for a further 30 days. Requires a passport valid at least 3 months from arrival, a confirmed onward/return ticket, and compulsory health insurance from a Ministry of Public Health-registered provider. The waiver is free of charge. GCC nationals (Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Saudi Arabia, UAE) enter without any visa on passport or GCC ID. The specific 90-day and 30-day country lists are published on the MOI portal but are rendered client-side and could not be extracted as verifiable text during this research.
policy_name: Visa-free entry / visa on arrival (visa waiver)

conditions: Holder of valid residence permit or entry visa in UK, USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Schengen, or GCC
Residence permit/entry visa valid at least 30 days
Passport valid at least 6 months
Proof of accommodation and return/onward ticket required
description: Facilitation allowing travellers of any nationality who hold a valid residence permit or entry visa in the UK, USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, a Schengen country, or a GCC nation to obtain a visa upon arrival. Grants a stay of up to 30 days, extendable online for another 30 days for the same visit. Requires proof of accommodation, a return/onward ticket, a passport valid at least 6 months, and the residence permit/entry visa valid at least 30 days. Applied for via www.qatarvisaservice.com.
maximum_stay: 30 days, extendable online for another 30 days
policy_name: Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA)

conditions: Applied for online via the Hayya platform prior to travel
Cost QAR 100
description: Nationalities not eligible for visa-free entry or an ETA apply before travel for a tourist visa through the official Hayya platform (hayya.qa / Hayya mobile app) at a cost of QAR 100. Hayya also handles GCC-resident and GCC-companion entry visas.
policy_name: Hayya tourist e-visa
